table_300_5_A.ref: Table 300.5(A) (2023 numbering; cited as 'Table 300.5' in earlier editions and on the current site)
table_300_5_A.status: verified-sd2023 for conditions 1-2 (SR-8551 is revised text in the A2022 Second Draft; two pulls agree; 6 planted canaries rejected). Condition 3 (checked 2026-10-24): 2022 Technical Meeting per-CAM results and Standards Council per-appeal decisions not seen. NFPA (blog, 31 Aug 2022): 55 CAMs; 14 appeals 'resulted in 18 amendments and four concurrently issuing' TIAs (by date, TIAs 23-3 to 23-6); appeal topics optical fiber cable, copper-clad aluminum wiring, surge protection devices, GFCI protection, swimming pool bonding. Overlap: none. Rendered as 2023 NEC under decision D-09. Row 1 (all locations not specified below), columns 1-4, is also VERIFIED-2023 (government paraphrase, three 2023 sources). EMT column placement UNVERIFIED (flattened headings)

rows.location: Under minimum of 102 mm (4 in.) thick concrete exterior slab with no vehicular traffic and the slab extending not less than 152 mm (6 in.) beyond the underground installation
rows.mapping_note: columns 4-5 mapping follows printed token order (two '150 6' then '(direct burial)' x2, two '100 4' then '(in raceway)' x2)

rows.location: Under streets, highways, roads, alleys, driveways, and parking lots
One- and two-family dwelling driveways and outdoor parking areas, and used only for dwelling-related purposes
In or under airport runways, including adjacent areas where trespassing is prohibited

footnotes.1: A lesser depth shall be permitted where specified in the installation instructions of a listed low-voltage lighting system.
footnotes.2: A depth of 150 mm (6 in.) shall be permitted for pool, spa, and fountain lighting, installed in a nonmetallic raceway, limited to not more than 30 volts where part of a listed low-voltage lighting system.

notes.1: Cover is [shall be] defined as the shortest distance in mm (in.) measured between a point on the top surface of any direct-buried conductor, cable, conduit, or other raceway and the top surface of finished grade, concrete, or similar cover. (verb flattened: 'is shall be')
notes.2: Raceways approved for burial only where concrete encased shall require a concrete envelope not less than 50 mm (2 in.) thick.
notes.3: Lesser depths shall be permitted where cables and conductors rise for terminations or splices or where access is otherwise required.
notes.4: Where one of the wiring method types listed in Columns 1 through 3 is used for one of the circuit types in Columns 4 and 5, the shallowest depth of burial shall be permitted.
notes.5: Where solid rock prevents compliance with the cover depths specified in this table, the wiring shall be installed in a metal raceway, or a nonmetallic raceway permitted for direct burial. The raceways shall be covered by a minimum of 50 mm (2 in.) of concrete extending down to rock.
notes.6: Directly buried electrical metallic tubing (EMT) shall comply with 358.10.

rule_300_5_D.status: Parent text: VERIFIED-draft (A2022 Second Draft SR-8553; single pull; TM check not done). (D)(1)-(4) values: VERIFIED-2023 (government paraphrase only); verbatim UNVERIFIED
rule_300_5_D.rule_summary: 2023 parent text (per SR-8553 and its statement): 'Conductors and cables shall be protected from damage in accordance with 300.5(D)(1) through (D)(4).' The word 'Direct-buried' was removed so the subdivisions also cover conductors in raceways. Government paraphrases of 2023: conductors emerging from grade protected by RMC, IMC or Schedule 80 PVC from 18 in below grade (or the minimum cover) to the point of termination above ground; warning ribbon at least 12 in above underground service conductors.

committee_statement_quote_segments: By removing the words “Direct-buried” from the parent text, the subdivisions will now cover conductors
whether they are in a raceway or are direct buried.
